raw_response:
I will not change too much from last year because 7 mu is not big, and if I spread myself too thin with risky changes, I lose money fast. I do wheat and maize as the backbone because that is the steady part of the year here, and I have well water, so I can protect yield when the weather turns dry. For wheat, I will keep fertilizer a little on the safe side because if wheat stands weak through winter and spring, I cannot get that yield back later. After wheat, I will put maize on the same land because that system fits my labor and water best. Cotton, mungbean, and red bean I will keep on smaller pieces. Cotton needs more watching and more sprays, but if I keep a small area I can manage it. Mungbean and red bean I do on lighter ground with less fertilizer because legumes do not eat fertilizer like maize and wheat do. I watch what people around me do, and I do not want to cut fertilizer too hard just to save a few yuan and then regret it at harvest. I will use rotary tillage on most land because it saves labor for my household of two, but I will plough the cotton piece once to loosen it better. Water I will give mainly to wheat, maize, and cotton. Beans I will water less unless the field really asks for it.
